items.title: Approve target architecture and registered research policy
items.scope: Review ARCHITECTURE.md and ADRs. Select initial universe, permitted data history/rights, horizons, availability plane, compute/storage budgets and task-specific primary score, meaningful margin, sample/calibration/coverage gates. Reserve a genuinely uninspected final chronological period and label-access rule before the first fit/feature comparison; if history is already seen, designate a later untouched/forward period instead.
items.acceptance: Explicit operator architecture approval and frozen benchmark policy exist before implementation/search. Unknowns and holdout-access policy are recorded; this issue must not be auto-completed by roadmap creation. Final-period reservation and access history are explicit; public historical availability alone does not make a previously inspected period untouched.

items.title: Specify additive v2 contracts and preserve v1 compatibility
items.scope: Inventory current datasets/jobs/providers/CLI, pin regression fixtures and define target/feature/distribution/experiment/task schemas and v1 adapters. Implement the minimal append-only trial/holdout-access ledger and protected final-range exclusion before any baseline fitting or ablation; M1/M2 use development data only.
items.acceptance: Old archive/dataset/forecast identities remain readable; unknown major versions fail closed; missing historical availability stays unknown; no in-place rewrite, lost pin or anchor reset. Review migration/rollback fixtures. Every early trial, failure, intervention and final-range access is recorded; early jobs cannot read reserved labels.

items.title: Add hourly through monthly return targets and PIT eligibility
items.scope: Choose and preregister source frequency, forecast cadence and sufficient permitted history per horizon. Add bounded deterministic finalized-bar resampling and duration/calendar-based v2 endpoint extraction for 1h/1d/7d/28d returns; preserve availability and raw lineage. Existing 1-128-step and 10,000-row v1 limits are not silently widened.
items.acceptance: A feasibility gate proves each horizon expressible with the chosen cadence, input history, matured train/validation/test counts and bounded resources before baseline work. Missing history blocks the affected capability. Resampling/gap/late-revision/time-quality fixtures pass; no look-ahead aggregation, manufactured bars or availability; v1 step/row caps remain intact.

items.title: Deliver chronological long-horizon baseline comparisons
items.scope: Add a minimal fixed baseline fit/evaluate task on the existing verified CPU launcher and durable job acceptance path: approved zero-return, train-only historical mean, regularized linear/AR and declared probabilistic algorithms. No arbitrary training endpoint. Extend chronological evaluation with common asset cutoffs, interval purge and justified embargo.
items.acceptance: Actual bounded baseline fit/evaluate runs under the qualified launcher; missing controls fail closed. Train-only transforms, label maturity, cancellation/recovery and negative leakage fixtures pass. Paired per-horizon scores/exclusions reproduce; service/CLI agree; baseline retained on null evidence; no advantage inferred from price-level fit. All comparisons use development ranges and the PI01 trial ledger, never the reserved final period.

items.title: Record forward forecasts before outcomes and score maturation

items.acceptance: Forecast accepted durably before outcome or marked late; duplicates/conflicts and restart preserve identity; immature labels are not scored; backcasts/replay/forward cannot be conflated; CLI/TUI services expose understandable status.

items.title: Qualify bounded analytical scans and native-engine choice

items.acceptance: Record full-job time/RSS/spill/bytes and semantic parity including exclusions; enforce file/network/extension/resource limits and cancellation; select minimum sufficient engine/version or retain current path. No invented capacity/Rust gain.

items.foundation_handover_requirements:
## Foundation handover — 2026-10-18

The operator explicitly consolidated the unfinished Foundation roadmap. Applicable requirements from F25/KER-29, F27/KER-31 and F29/KER-33 remain mandatory here:

- Provide bounded read-only health/alerts/collection/coverage reporting through a peer-authorized Unix facade or an equivalently restricted local application service. Permit only approved fields/methods; reject unauthorized/oversized input. The reporting principal cannot mutate collector configuration/state, launch jobs, resolve secrets or choose arbitrary paths/SQL; reports cannot starve collection.
- Demonstrate manual clean-host installation on the declared Linux profile, dedicated identities and fixed collector/transfer/parser/model roles, credential/time prerequisites, effective-control probes and restart/reboot resumption. No automatic privileged installer or generic elevation helper.
- Operator-only retention/pruning previews protect dataset/model/evidence pins, manifests and trust anchors. Disk pressure fails safely; independent backup restore reproduces dataset/anchor; migration and failed-upgrade rollback preserve history or require an explicit new epoch. No rollback-induced chain/sequence reuse.

Telegram-specific methods/units are optional, outside the core gate. Superseding old tasks is not implementation completion; keep this task Backlog and preserve its existing blockers.

items.scope: Source/provider/task conformance, installed profiles, operator/incident runbooks, glossary and shared service/CLI/TUI workflows.
items.acceptance: A bounded extra source/family and provider/task exercise passes relevant contracts without unrelated restructuring; installation/help work headlessly; meaningful failures and cancellation are consistent; documentation reflects delivered evidence only.

items.foundation_handover_requirements:
## Foundation release-gate handover — 2026-10-18

The original Foundation v1 release was not completed. Its applicable reliability/security qualification is retained in this redesigned core gate, in addition to the predictive/worker/private-UX requirements already below:

- At least 72 hours of continuous public-data collection on the declared workload/profile, injecting network disconnects and graceful/forced restarts. Account for every locally committed input as archived, pending or explicitly rejected; bound queue/memory/disk growth and expose observed/unknown gaps. This does not establish universal scale.
- Simulate the configured offline horizon and retention volume with fixtures, then reconnect a separate workstation. Verify repeated/interrupted pull, corrupt objects, history conflicts and local-anchor recovery. A 72-hour soak does not prove a 90-day retention envelope.
- Clean locked build/install and installed profiles; admitted model/dependency inventory; unit, adapter, integration, crash/recovery, hostile-input, secret-redaction, effective OS-control and import-boundary checks; dataset/replay rebuild and operator/extension documentation. Missing critical evidence blocks release; revised policy must not silently erase a failed criterion.
- Demonstrate systemd restart/reboot, degraded clock, disk pressure and independent backup restore. Model/UI/optional notification failures must not stop healthy collection. Real credentials remain absent from CI and are limited to approved operator-controlled smoke tests where required.

Telegram delivery is optional and excluded from prediction-core completion. Core readiness does not require profitable forecasts. Keep Backlog; Foundation cancellation does not qualify either release.

items.title: Specify shared AI-client capability and approval contracts
items.scope: Define a small transport-neutral application-service contract for authenticated subject/client context, capability/object visibility, typed DTOs, opaque object IDs, pagination/errors, idempotent admission and canonical configuration preview/approval/apply/rollback. Map the proposed MCP surface to existing Services workflows and identify absent common service support. Freeze conservative numeric quotas and allowed configuration fields. Documentation/schema/fixture contract only; no MCP runtime dependency. This is an independent branch after admitted training/qualification, not a prerequisite for early forecasting or model comparisons.
items.acceptance: Reviewed operation-to-service/capability/data-class matrix covers read-only, preauthorized operations and narrow management. Caller identity never comes from tool arguments/_meta. DTO/schema fixtures exclude arbitrary paths, SQL, URLs, code, secrets, roles/security-policy changes, hidden qualification data, promotion and trading. The approval contract binds authenticated subject/client/action, exact normalized diff hash, base revision, target scope, policy version, expiry and single-use durable consumption; client confirmations cannot mint approval. Define cumulative budget/idempotency/cancel semantics, safe error/output caps and resource ACLs. Preserve v1 readers and existing service/CLI/TUI behavior; no new dependency on PI02–PI04 or PI21.

items.title: Add optional read-only MCP adapter and local/private transports
items.scope: Implement the optional official-protocol Python adapter over the authenticated private application facade. Expose authorized health/catalog/source/data-quality/model/compute and released forecast/report/comparison/job views plus fixed documentation/schema resources. Start with operator-managed stdio; add a separately qualified authenticated private Streamable HTTP profile. Pin/review official SDK and transitive licenses/lock impact. No new business logic or durable MCP store; no operational mutation tools in this task.
items.acceptance: Read-only schemas and structured/text responses, bounded bytes/rows/deadlines, caller-bound paging/cache and direct resource ACLs pass contract tests. SDK auth is explicitly configured and tested for issuer/subject/client/resource/audience/scope, Origin/Host and proxy trust; SDK defaults and annotations do not prove security. Current stateless discovery and explicitly supported older initialize/session profiles are tested separately; unsupported versions/capabilities fail safely. Secrets/hidden labels/raw paths/raw exceptions are absent, including diagnostic/error cases. Adapter is an optional separate process/package; concurrent request ownership and kill/disconnect/auth outage do not close shared services or stop collection/forecast/CLI. Read-only enablement requires its scoped client/security evidence; management remains disabled pending PI28/PI29.

items.title: Expose bounded MCP operations and approved configuration changes
items.scope: Map allowed forecast/research submission, owned-job inspection/cancellation and narrow validated configuration proposals/apply/rollback to existing application management. Use immutable registered dataset/recipe/model/task IDs and operator-approved aggregate resource/trial policies. Forecast models must already be production-eligible; research candidates gain no promotion authority. Human-sensitive changes use trusted CLI/TUI/private-dashboard approval of authoritative diffs; MCP cannot approve itself.
items.acceptance: Unauthorized/forged/out-of-scope inputs have no mutation. Idempotent admission persists one receipt before acknowledgement; lost replies/retries recover by owner/key and conflicting manifests fail. Explicit cancellation preserves existing durable job states and cannot cancel another owner; invocation disconnect does not cancel accepted jobs. Approval deny/expiry/replay/client-subject substitution/diff alteration/stale revision/policy drift/concurrent apply and crash recovery preserve one audited outcome. Rollback revalidates/reapproves reversible changes and does not claim to undo consumed compute or exposed data. Cumulative multi-client CPU/GPU/time/storage/concurrency/trial quotas, sealed-holdout/research/qualification boundaries, pre-outcome forecasts and secret redaction remain enforced by shared services. No shell/SQL/filesystem/install/security-policy/enrollment/promotion/trading endpoint.

items.title: Qualify MCP trust boundaries and real client interoperability
items.scope: Run the canonical MCP security/failure-isolation/client matrix on synthetic/public fixtures. Record exact server/SDK/protocol/client build/surface/account policy and transport. Qualify nominated Codex CLI/IDE and Claude Code local stdio/private HTTP separately; evaluate ChatGPT direct HTTPS versus Secure MCP Tunnel and hosted Claude only for separately authorized available deployments. No broad compatibility claim from SDK selection or offline protocol fixtures.
items.acceptance: Evidence covers unauthorized mutations/resources, forged metadata, injection/malformed/oversized inputs, traversal/SSRF/unsafe metadata redirects, output/secret/holdout filtering, approval/configuration races, cumulative quotas, two principals/connections, cancellation/completion/lost reply/restart, audit integrity/failure/restore and adapter/auth/tunnel/slow-client/flood isolation while core services continue. Real nominated client tests verify discovery/pagination/schema/text+structured output/resources where supported, OAuth login/refresh/revoke/scopes/actual callback registration and supported protocol fallback; confirm client allow settings cannot replace server approval. Mark unavailable/unsupported profiles explicitly; record provider/data-export and ingress/egress decisions before hosted tests. Enable only evidence-qualified capability/profile combinations, retain disable/rollback procedure, and leave existing PI21 release dependencies intact.
